pages.text: It rained all night, and in the morning the street was a brown river. Eli could not go to school. He stood at the window of Hamdia’s house and watched sandals, bottles and a plastic bucket float by. “Can we go out and play in it?” he asked. “No,” said Hamdia’s mother, and she said it very gently, but very firmly.
sentences: It rained all night, and in the morning the street was a brown river.
Eli could not go to school.
He stood at the window of Hamdia’s house and watched sandals, bottles and a plastic bucket float by.
“Can we go out and play in it?” he asked.
“No,” said Hamdia’s mother, and she said it very gently, but very firmly.
pages.alt: A boy looks from a window at a brown flooded street where bottles and a bucket float by.

pages.text: “Come here,” said Hamdia’s mother. She pointed to the street. “Do you see where the water is smooth? Under it is an open drain. In floods, brown water hides open drains and holes. A child can fall in, even if they know the road.” Eli swallowed. “So the water has a secret.” “Yes,” she said. “Water under the water.”

“Water under the water.”
pages.alt: A cut-away picture of a street with brown water on top and a hidden open drain beneath.

pages.text: She told them the flood rules. “Do not wade or play in floodwater. Do not walk near fast water. Stay away from fuel, wires and anything that sparks. If someone is in danger, shout for an adult. Never go in yourself.” Hamdia wrote each rule in her notebook and drew a picture beside it.

If someone is in danger, shout for an adult.
Never go in yourself.” Hamdia wrote each rule in her notebook and drew a picture beside it.
pages.alt: A child’s notebook with a list of flood rules and small pictures of a no-entry sign and an adult.

pages.text: “Floodwater is dirty,” said Hamdia’s mother. “It carries rubbish, mud and germs from the street. Sometimes it gets into wells or drinking water. Then people can get very sick with diseases like cholera and diarrhoea. A doctor in Sunyani says that cholera spreads when floodwater gets into drinking water. Children under five are most at risk.” Eli looked at the water drum. “Is ours safe?”

“Is ours safe?”
pages.alt: A diagram showing dirty floodwater approaching a covered water drum and a cup of clean water.

pages.text: “It is safe because we keep it covered,” she said. “We use a clean cup with a handle. We wash our hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet. If the water looks cloudy, we boil it or treat it, and we keep the drum shut.” She showed them the lid. “These are small things, but small things protect big people.”

“These are small things, but small things protect big people.”
pages.alt: A covered water drum with a clean cup and a bar of soap beside a hand-washing station.

pages.text: “And when the flood goes,” she said, “it leaves pools. Still water is where mosquitoes lay eggs. We empty buckets and tyres, clear the gutter by the gate and cover our water. A clean yard helps stop malaria.” Hamdia nodded. “That is why our teacher says never to throw rubbish in the drain,” she said. “It keeps the water moving.”

pages.text: “Mama,” said Eli, “why do we not cover the open drain?” “That is a very good question,” said Hamdia’s mother. “It is not our drain to cover. It belongs to the Assembly. Families can ask, politely and together. Children can help by drawing, counting and writing down what they see.” Eli took a pencil. “I will draw the drain,” he said. “And we will write it down.”

pages.text: When the rain stopped, the water went down slowly. Eli and Hamdia did not go out until an adult said it was safe. Then they helped their neighbours. They carried dry cloth, shared bread, and poured out puddles from buckets. “We are not strong,” said Eli, “but we can be careful.” Hamdia smiled. “And kind,” she said. The end.

activities.prompt: Floodwater can get into drinking water. What should we do to keep our water safe?
options: Keep it covered and use a clean cup

activities.question: What can children do about an open drain?
options: Ask politely and help by drawing and counting

items: Keep drinking water covered and clean.
After the flood, empty puddles and help neighbours.
